messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Cut points for movisens data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jo,

I had an e-mail conversation this week with someone asking the same question (same group?). Below I have copied a summary of the conversation to enable you and others to learn from my answers:

Question 27 June by student in Australia

We are presently using the Movisens EcgMove4 to capture movement in our study to determine how it may influence emotion regulation ability and the experience of psychological symptoms. The Movisens sensor is worn on the chest during a selected 12-hour waking period for 10 days.

Having processed the data, we've noticed the outputs show very high volumes of inactivity (around 89-95%) in a 18–65-year-old sample. I've attached an example output here (please note this output is from before applying the Eisgler 2011 modification). We've tried the Eisgler (2011) syntax modification (as below), but this resulted in no output for light, moderate or vigorous activity. We've tried changing the 'SampleRateInStudy' value to 64 (to match Movisens hz), using 'part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE, but still no output was produced for light, moderate or vigorous activity. I'm wondering if you might be able to provide any advice or assistance with this issue?

Response 28 June by me

Regarding the thresholds, I am now in doubt whether the information we have in the vignette is correct. The paper by Esliger was not very clear and did not come with code if I remember correctly. I now think we need to divide instead of multiply by 60. So, the calculation then becomes:

threshold.lig = ((LightCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

threshold.mod = ((ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

threshold.vig = ((VigorousCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

mvpathreshold = ((ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

which could be re-written in a more readable way as:

threshold.lig = (LightCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

threshold.mod = (ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

threshold.vig = (VigorousCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

mvpathreshold = (ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

I never used these equations myself and nobody provided feedback on this, so I assumed that people were happy with the equations.

Further, it may also be good for you to try out the other cut-points designed for data collected on the hip and compare results. If they all result in a high amounts of time spent in inactivity then this may indicate that hip cut points in general are not ideal for chest-worn sensors. If only some cut-points overestimate time in inactivity then it seems more likely that it is a study specific issue, e..g. they used a different calculation or they more calibration error in their data.

...

The conversation that followed clarified that their sleep estimates where problematic, most likely as a result of accelerometers not being worn. We then had some interaction about how to improve the sleep detection.

Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.body_plain:
First of all, thanks a lot for making GGIR possible and all the hard work that must have gone into it. It's much appreciated.

I am using it to process GENEActiv .bin files which contain data for several days. My main objective is to identify the number of valid hours for each day. For that purpose, I've run parts 1 and 2 with qwindow = c(0, 24). I am using the "part2_daysummary" CSV for my analysis.

When checking the output I noticed unexpected results in the "calendar_date" and "N hours" columns. An example is attached. It appears that there is an issue with the last day, which happens consistently across 60 analysed files.

The example shows recorded GENEActiv data for 15 days. This is accurately captured in the "measurementday" column. However, in the "calendar_date" column the last entry appears to be wrong. I expected 2020-12-26T00:00:00+0000 but it is recorded as 2020-12-25T23:59:55+0000. Furthermore, the "N hours" column says the day had 24.001 hours.

This pattern appears consistently across all 60 files - the last day always has 24.001 hours and the date incorrectly shows as a duplicate of the previous day at T23:59:55.

My code:

GGIR(datadir = "path to several GENEActiv .bin files",
     outputdir = "path to output folder",
     mode = 1:2, # Run GGIR parts 1 and 2
     do.report = 2, # Generate csv-report for GGIR part 2
     qwindow = c(0, 24)) # Analyse midnight to midnight (full day segments only)

Have I overlooked something or is this a bug?

Best regards,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Data merging
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nury,

> We want to know how the GGIR package identifies the Start Time when reading the csv file?

GGIR uses the first timestamp and then assumes that time during the rest of the recording can be derived from the sampling frequency. For some brands (Axivity) and optionally with the ad-hoc csv file by setting rmc.doresample=TRUE. we interpolate (resample) the data points to have consistent sample frequency. So, what you are probably missing is in your effort to append the csv files is a step to omit overlapping timestamps (if this applies). Als you may want to set  rmc.check4timegaps = TRUE which fills in the time gaps.

> Finally, We would like to konw, is there a  way in GGIR to solve the problem of merging gt3x files?
>

GGIR does not facilitate merging gt3x files. You could try ask the Actigraph company.

> Please forgive me if I ask any stupid question.

Questions are never stupid. It is good for GGIR if everyone posts their questions/challenges here such that we can all learn from them.

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mayan,

> I thought I had figured out the coding but it just doesn't seem to work, it isn't deleting any of the data...

Your arguments are correct, but your expectation of what they do is not not. They tell GGIR to treat those time segments as invalid, which is not the same as deleting them. Invalid data is not counted towards the accelerometer wear time, and invalid data is imputed when performing analysis. Days with a large amount of invalid data are skipped in the result.

Once you have create your .csv daysummary reports:
part2_daysummary.csv shows all days, it is up to you as user to delete the rows you consider of less relevant.
part2_summary.csv accounts for missing/invalid days, so days with missing data have been excluded.
results/part4_nightsummary_cleaned.csv is free of invalid days.
results/part5_daysummary_....csv is free of invalid days.
The day/night summary files in results/QC folder do include the invalid days.

For the .pdf visualisations I am afraid GGIR is not extremely flexible in this respect. I have always focussed on the quantitative output and regarded the pdf as a helpful way to QC the data, where missing data is actually useful to be informed about. That said, I imagine major enhancements are possible on the visualisation side of GGIR for which it would be good to have people/funding to work on.

Cheers,

Vincent

Any thoughts on how bad this might be or any alternatives are welcome!
